operations.title: Codimension-one Kummer branch chain-lift underdetermination test
operations.method: Read the frozen 32-to-16 branch census and compare distinct positive integral linear lifts compatible with sheet-label coalescence and selected positive-chain normalization.

operations.title: Five-site codimension-one sheet coalescence does not determine the physical relative-chain pushforward
operations.body: Entry 1224's bit-mask quotient proves 32-to-16 label coalescence and generic deck orientation preservation, but no boundary-compatible specialization or multiplicity. Positive integral lifts with negative-sheet multiplicities 1 and 2 both satisfy the recorded label, positivity, and selected positive-chain normalization; only multiplicity one satisfies full coefficient-Betti adjunction, which is itself not source-admitted.

operations.outcome: pass: frozen branch census is 32-to-16; two distinct positive integral lifts satisfy recorded evidence; adjunction defects are respectively 0 and 1

evidence.paraphrase: Exact audit exhibits nonunique positive chain lifts and isolates the extra adjunction assumption.

operations.title: Grothendieck isolates the missing five-site branch-chain multiplicity
operations.body: I attacked the codimension-one branch C2->1 as the first possible physical lift. The frozen checker implements branch restriction only as bit masking and counts 32->16 sheet classes. It supplies no relative-pair map, boundary operator, or specialization multiplicity. After fixing Gamma_+->Gamma and retaining positive orientation, Gamma_->Gamma and Gamma_->2Gamma are both compatible with the recorded label quotient and selected normalization; only the first satisfies full coefficient-Betti adjunction. Therefore multiplicity one is algebraically canonical after assuming adjunction, but is not physically derivable from Entry 1224 without circularity. The precise requested source datum is a boundary-compatible specialization of relative pairs with local degree/intersection multiplicity and endpoint/regulator normalization.
